title: New Hebrides
capsule: The New Hebrides Condominium was a uniquely anomalous colonial arrangement under which Britain and France jointly administered the archipelago in the southwest Pacific from 1906, following a protocol that established parallel but separate British and French legal, administrative, and judicial systems for their respective nationals, with indigenous ni-Vanuatu people subject to neither. The arrangement was formalized by the Anglo-French Protocol of 1914 and created notorious administrative paralysis; the island group had three currencies, three court systems, and two police forces. A joint independence movement culminated in the Republic of Vanuatu on 30 July 1980.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The New Hebrides archipelago is geographically well-defined; colonial administrative boundaries and the extent of effective control versus nominal sovereignty over individual islands are documented in British and French colonial records.
